topic: SC: counter-bought railway tickets to get the same insurance as online tickets from 27 Oct 2026 (Union of India v. Radha Yadav)

slides.title: Counter tickets get **insurance** too
slides.subtitle: Until now, only online buyers could get travel cover. From **27 October**, tickets bought at the station window must get it as well.
slides.cite: **Union of India v. Radha Yadav**, 2026 LiveLaw (SC) 1047 · Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah & Justice R. Mahadevan

slides.label: The problem
slides.title: Online vs offline: **unequal** cover
bullets: Passengers booking online could buy travel insurance by paying a **small extra amount**.
Passengers buying at the station counter had **no such option** at all.
The amicus curiae told the Court the Railways had taken **no action** on the issue.

slides.label: What the Court ordered
slides.title: Implement it within two weeks
bullets: From **27.10.2026**, every ticket sold over the counter at all stations must carry insurance, just like online tickets.
The order is **mandatory**. If it is not followed, the **Railway Board** is directly responsible.
The Court had earlier given the Railways **time** to find a way to cover offline buyers, including the poorest passengers. Nothing had moved.

slides.label: Railways pulled up
slides.title: Promises only on **paper**
bullets: The Court said the assurances were largely on paper, and the passenger-safety budget had **not been fully used**.
The Railway Board Chairman and members must **appear in person** on **16 November 2026**.
If work is not seen on the ground, they may be held **personally responsible**.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: What we **don't know** yet
bullets: The **premium and cover amount** for counter tickets are not stated in the reports. Watch for the Railways' notification.
The order takes effect from 27 October. It does not automatically apply to journeys before that.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.
slides.note: Law fact: Compensation for a train accident or **untoward incident** is a separate claim under the Railways Act, 1989 — **Section 124A** (Railway Claims Tribunal).

slides.title: Know the law, know your **rights**
lines: One important ruling every day, in simple words.
**Save** this, and **share** it with anyone who travels by train.

caption:
Buy your train ticket at the station counter? This one is for you 🚆⚖️

Until now, railway travel insurance was available only to passengers booking online. Those buying at the counter — many of them poor and rural travellers — were left without that protection.

The Supreme Court has directed the Railways that from 27 October 2026, every ticket sold over the counter at all stations must carry insurance cover just like online tickets. The order is mandatory, and the Railway Board will be directly responsible if it is not followed.

The Court was unhappy that the passenger-safety budget had not been fully used, and has called the Railway Board Chairman and members to appear in person on 16 November. The premium and cover amount are yet to be announced — keep an eye out for the Railways' notification.

Case: Union of India v. Radha Yadav, 2026 LiveLaw (SC) 1047
Bench: Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah & Justice R. Mahadevan

This post is for information only, not legal advice.
